description:
Piracy Reworked

v0.1.0 - the underworld runs on your money - for Starsector 0.98a-RC8

Download

PiracyReworked-0.1.0.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher. Safe to add to an existing save.

Pogo's explanation

Basically i didnt like how pirate bases were random and infinite, in that no matter how many you destroy another pops up. I also dont like how the core early game loop of starsector is to buy and sell exclusively on the black market with near zero consequences. So in a nutshell the core concept is the more black market stuff you do the richer the pirates get and the more bases they can afford, which leads to them snowballing with more raids, more profits from raids -> more bases again etc etc. Obviously you can keep them under control by wiping out their bases, so you offset your ledger so to speak.

There's a bunch of other features but this is the gist of it. Once the pirates get wealthy enough the 'Piracy Respite' earned from defeating the colony crisis wont be enough to stop them messing with your shipping, and they will wreak havoc on the stability of the core worlds. Bounties also get put on your head for any piracy action you do with transponder on, but it wont be evident to you this has happened until the bounty is large enough.

Claude's explanation

Every black-market transaction (buy or sell, transponder on or off) feeds a sector-wide pirate war chest. Sales are weighted by usefulness to a war effort - weapons x3, ships x2, commodities x1, ore x0.5, plus a bonus for blueprints. Wash-trading nets to zero.The war chest is a real economy: operating bases earn passive income, launching a raid costs credits per fleet point, a successful raid pays spoils with interest, a repelled raid is a pure loss, and when the chest covers the next base's price (~94k to ~614k by tier) the pirates expand.Strategy loop: smuggle and the underworld snowballs, repel raids and it stagnates at break-even, hunt bases and it shrinks.Underworld tithe: a monthly cut of the whole sector's illegal trade keeps pirates financed late game regardless of your own habits. Your colonies are clients, and free ports (yours included) fence at a multiplier.The broker: underworld contacts source real installed colony items (removed from the victim colony on success, priced by the source's defenses) and a rotating monthly menu of rare blueprints. Deposits go straight to the war chest and count as your patronage; fulfillment is a real raid resolved by the raid sim.Fading wariness: past the thresholds (500k lifetime / 25% share by default) chest-funded bases resume the pirate-activity condition on your colonies; laying off restores the respite and hunting pirates offsets your ledger.A price on your head: factions whose markets you smuggle through post personal bounties (no rep impact), gated on vanilla smuggling suspicion. Freelance hunters collect off the combined price, scale with the pool, and can hunt several at once; a decoy fleet freezes a bounty.Tier 3+ bases field extra medium/heavy patrols, bigger fleets and a tier-scaled garrison.The "Pirate War Chest" intel screen is a full balance sheet - chest, income streams, operating bases, savings toward the next base, recent ledger, and how much of the pirate economy you bankrolled.Machine factions (Remnants and their like) are outside the underworld economy: no tithe, no commission raids, no bounties.Keeps vanilla per-base raid strength and cadence, tier progression, station restoration, the post-kill respawn freeze and the first-year grace period.For Starsector 0.98a-RC8. LunaLib optional (live in-game config menu; otherwise reads data/config/settings.json). Vanilla-only, no hard dependencies. Safe to add to an existing save.

Recommended mod collection for ultimate late game experience

Standalone, safe to add mid-save, can be run together or separately.

Threat Incursion — the threat colonizes the sector and invades the core worlds. Disrupt their supply chains and besiege the entrenched hives into decline.
Commerce Wars — dominate a faction's markets or the military balance and they push back: ultimatums, tribute, enforcement fleets.
Piracy Reworked — the underworld runs on your money: black-market trade funds a self-sustaining pirate war economy.
Remnant Retribution — a late-game colony crisis.
Useful Planetary Shield — planetary shields finally do something: they absorb orbital bombardment.

Disclaimer: This post and mod were written using Claude's Fable AI model.

Piracy Reworked
v0.1.0 - the underworld runs on your money - for Starsector 0.98a-RC8

Download

PiracyReworked-0.1.0.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher. Safe to add to an existing save.


Pogo's explanation

Basically i didnt like how pirate bases were random and infinite, in that no matter how many you destroy another pops up. I also dont like how the core early game loop of starsector is to buy and sell exclusively on the black market with near zero consequences. So in a nutshell the core concept is the more black market stuff you do the richer the pirates get and the more bases they can afford, which leads to them snowballing with more raids, more profits from raids -> more bases again etc etc. Obviously you can keep them under control by wiping out their bases, so you offset your ledger so to speak.

There's a bunch of other features but this is the gist of it. Once the pirates get wealthy enough the 'Piracy Respite' earned from defeating the colony crisis wont be enough to stop them messing with your shipping, and they will wreak havoc on the stability of the core worlds. Bounties also get put on your head for any piracy action you do with transponder on, but it wont be evident to you this has happened until the bounty is large enough.


Claude's explanation

  • Every black-market transaction (buy or sell, transponder on or off) feeds a sector-wide pirate war chest. Sales are weighted by usefulness to a war effort - weapons x3, ships x2, commodities x1, ore x0.5, plus a bonus for blueprints. Wash-trading nets to zero.
  • The war chest is a real economy: operating bases earn passive income, launching a raid costs credits per fleet point, a successful raid pays spoils with interest, a repelled raid is a pure loss, and when the chest covers the next base's price (~94k to ~614k by tier) the pirates expand.
  • Strategy loop: smuggle and the underworld snowballs, repel raids and it stagnates at break-even, hunt bases and it shrinks.
  • Underworld tithe: a monthly cut of the whole sector's illegal trade keeps pirates financed late game regardless of your own habits. Your colonies are clients, and free ports (yours included) fence at a multiplier.
  • The broker: underworld contacts source real installed colony items (removed from the victim colony on success, priced by the source's defenses) and a rotating monthly menu of rare blueprints. Deposits go straight to the war chest and count as your patronage; fulfillment is a real raid resolved by the raid sim.
  • Fading wariness: past the thresholds (500k lifetime / 25% share by default) chest-funded bases resume the pirate-activity condition on your colonies; laying off restores the respite and hunting pirates offsets your ledger.
  • A price on your head: factions whose markets you smuggle through post personal bounties (no rep impact), gated on vanilla smuggling suspicion. Freelance hunters collect off the combined price, scale with the pool, and can hunt several at once; a decoy fleet freezes a bounty.
  • Tier 3+ bases field extra medium/heavy patrols, bigger fleets and a tier-scaled garrison.
  • The "Pirate War Chest" intel screen is a full balance sheet - chest, income streams, operating bases, savings toward the next base, recent ledger, and how much of the pirate economy you bankrolled.
  • Machine factions (Remnants and their like) are outside the underworld economy: no tithe, no commission raids, no bounties.
  • Keeps vanilla per-base raid strength and cadence, tier progression, station restoration, the post-kill respawn freeze and the first-year grace period.
  • For Starsector 0.98a-RC8. LunaLib optional (live in-game config menu; otherwise reads data/config/settings.json). Vanilla-only, no hard dependencies. Safe to add to an existing save.


Recommended mod collection for ultimate late game experienceStandalone, safe to add mid-save, can be run together or separately.
  • Threat Incursion — the threat colonizes the sector and invades the core worlds. Disrupt their supply chains and besiege the entrenched hives into decline.
  • Commerce Wars — dominate a faction's markets or the military balance and they push back: ultimatums, tribute, enforcement fleets.
  • Piracy Reworked — the underworld runs on your money: black-market trade funds a self-sustaining pirate war economy.
  • Remnant Retribution — a late-game colony crisis.
  • Useful Planetary Shield — planetary shields finally do something: they absorb orbital bombardment.

The system creates a feedback loop where smuggling increases pirate strength, while hunting their bases or repelling raids reduces it. Features include personal bounties for piracy actions, a detailed intel screen showing the pirate balance sheet, and integration with colony stability mechanics.
